comparisons.peer_topic: Unsecured Funding Profile and Credit Rating Covenants
comparisons.peer_summary: The company issues long-term unsecured debt to manage maturity profiles and mitigate refinancing risk, noting that while funding costs may be impacted by market conditions, substantially all debt obligations lack provisions triggering early repayment or additional collateral requirements based on adverse changes in credit ratings or financial ratios.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose information regarding their long-term unsecured debt funding and direct readers to specific notes for further details on subordinated and other long-term debt structures. JPM explicitly references subordinated debt and points to Note 20, while BAC describes its strategy of issuing long-term unsecured debt (including subordinated obligations) to manage maturity profiles and explicitly references Note 11 for details on long-term debt funding. Both filings highlight the role of subordinated/unsecured debt in their capital management and provide cross-references to financial statement notes for deeper disclosure.

sentences.text: Refer to Long-term funding on page 114 and Note 20 for additional information on the Firm's subordinated debt.
We issue long-term unsecured debt in a variety of maturities and currencies to achieve cost-efficient funding and to maintain an appropriate maturity profile.
For more information on long-term debt funding, including issuances and maturities and redemptions, see Note 11 - Long-term Debt to the Consolidated Financial Statements.
